The _example_* entries show every field and are ignored by the scripts. Field meanings: verification/rules/PIPELINE.md (stage/reason table, naming) and VERDICTS.md. paper.title: A short note on three elementary inequalities

defs._note: No shared Lean definitions file is needed: this note's only shared notation (R, R_{>0}, S(x,y,z)) is elementary enough to inline per-statement; see verification/INVENTORY.md section 4.

results.title: AM-GM for two reals
results.label: lem:amgm
results.summary_en: AM-GM for two reals (ab ≤ (a²+b²)/2, equality iff a=b): fully verified, no conditions.

results.title: Nesbitt-type refinement
results.label: prop:nesbitt
results.summary_en: Nesbitt-type refinement (S(x,y,z) ≥ 3(xy+yz+zx)/(2(x²+y²+z²)) for x,y,z>0): verified, conditional on Nesbitt's inequality (cited, Nesbitt1903 Thm 1), used via L01 (UNCONDITIONAL).

results.title: quotient inequality
results.label: lem:quot
results.summary_en: Lemma 2.3 revised (x > -1): x^2/(1+x) >= x-1 fully verified, no conditions; the printed statement now excludes the x < -1 region where the pre-revision text was false (B01), and the proof's sign-fact step (1+x>0) is now explicit.

history.partial: No clause of L02 is verified unconditionally or conditionally; the printed statement itself is false on x < -1. The restricted statement (x > -1) was independently checked as true and provable along the source's own route (see audit), but that is not what the paper prints, so it is not registered as a separate verified result.
history.summary_en: Lemma 2.3 (x²/(1+x) ≥ x-1 for x≠-1) is false as printed: counterexample x=-2 gives -4≥-3, which fails. ERROR, confirmed by independent counterexample review. Does not affect L01 or P01.

external_tools.meaning: Nesbitt-type bound S(x,y,z) = x/(y+z)+y/(z+x)+z/(x+y) ≥ 3/2 for all positive reals x,y,z
external_tools.mathlib_search: not searched in mathlib (external literature citation, not a request to mathlib); drafter/gate treated it as the paper's own cited external result, specialized exactly as main.tex:60 states it, no stronger
external_tools.human_check: confirm Nesbitt's inequality S(x,y,z) ≥ 3/2 for x,y,z>0 is indeed Theorem 1 of A. M. Nesbitt, Problem 15114, Educational Times 55 (1903), 37, as cited; this is a 19th-century problem-column item (priority B on the human-check worksheet per EDITORIAL note from the gate: citation attribution/numbering of an old problem column is the kind of thing worth a second look)

human_checked.how: Nesbitt, Problem 15114, Educational Times 55 (1903), and the standard proof by the rearrangement inequality
